newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Aug inflation matches post-unification low.
newsitem.headline: German Aug inflation matches post-unification low.

text.p: German inflation in August equalled a post-unification record low of 1.4 percent after falling from 1.6 percent in July, the Federal Statistics Office said Tuesday.
Annual inflation equalled June's record low after prices fell by 0.1 percent in August.

The annual inflation rate in western Germany edged up by one-tenth of a percentage point to 1.4 percent. That was offset by a drop in east Germany to 1.8 percent from 3.0 percent, as rent hikes from summer 1995 dropped out of the data series.
One regional central banker said Monday he did not expect the outlook for German prices to deteriorate despite a pickup in economic activity in the second quarter of this year.
Ernst Welteke, chairman of the Hessen central bank, said that an economic revival would not necessarily cloud the price outlook.

"From that point of view we should not expect a turnaround in interest rate developments," Welteke told foreign bankers in Frankfurt. The German Bundesbank last cut its key repo interest rate to 3 percent on Aug. 22.

Separate trade data released Tuesday showed that Germany's trade surplus fell in June to seven billion marks ($4.66 billion) from 9.5 billion marks ($6.33 billion) in May. It was still one billion marks ($666 million) higher in the first half of 1996 at 45.5 billion marks ($30.3 billion).

The current account deficit fell in June to 2.1 billion marks ($1.4 billion) after a 2.5 billion mark ($1.66 billion) shortfall in May. But the cumulative six-month deficit more than doubled, rising to 8.8 billion marks ($5.86 billion) against 4.1 billion marks ($2.73 billion) in first half 1995.
